mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25% per month for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 YoY change falls below -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE < 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their previous 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are above their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both below 12-month moving averages for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST are below their 12-month moving averages for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which in a late-cycle economy increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS above 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months in a late-cycle regime (UNRATE < 4%).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% signals a supply-side expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO > 12-month moving average +1.5% AND CPIAUCSL YoY <= 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO jumps above its 12-month moving average by more than 1.5% and CPIAUCSL YoY <= 4%.
